title: Dynamic scope binding and privilege resolution spec for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a deterministic, auditable privilege resolution model for RBAC v2 that supports dynamic scope binding across resource hierarchies, integrates with SSO/SAML assertions, emits rich audit events for every decision, and provides admin controls including emergency breakglass and scoped delegation. This ticket captures design goals, concrete resolution algorithms, example matrices, migration considerations, and operational hooks for the Console and runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A clear, unambiguous permission evaluation order that covers role inheritance, scope overrides, deny/allow precedence, and attribute-based exceptions.
Mapping rules from SAML attributes / OIDC claims to role assignments and scope anchors with deterministic precedence documented.
Audit event schema defined for: role assignment changes, resolved permissions per request, scope-binding decisions, and breakglass activations.
Admin UI wireframes and API endpoints for scoped delegation, role previews, and one-click breakglass with TTL and justification tracking.
A migration plan with compatibility mode for existing RBAC v1 tokens and a rollout checklist for Dedicated/Private clusters.
design_summary: Core idea: treat scopes as first-class, namespaced bindings that can be static (tenant-level) or dynamic (request-bound). At request time, the system builds a 'scope stack' by walking the resource hierarchy from requested resource to tenancy root, collecting explicit scope bindings and evaluating them with an ordered algorithm: 1) explicit deny at nearest scope, 2) explicit allow at nearest scope, 3) role-derived permissions (closest scope wins), 4) attribute-based grants (SAML/OIDC claim-driven) as tie-breakers, 5) global defaults. Roles are declarative sets of actions tied to resource classes; role-templates may be parameterized by scope variables (e.g., project_id). For SSO/SAML, attributes map to initial role assignments and to ephemeral request attributes (group, department, external_project). These attributes have a precedence table: direct role assignment > SAML-group assignment > SCIM-synced group > OIDC claim. Audit events must capture the fully expanded permission set and the evaluation trace (scope anchors, rules hit, deny/allow source). Breakglass is implemented as a short-lived override token issued by the Console with mandatory justification recorded; breakglass tokens are revoked automatically and emit both creation and use audit events.
implementation_steps: Spec review and alignment with Product and Security (1 week): finalize evaluation order and SAML claim mappings.
Schema changes: extend role binding table with 'scope_kind' and 'binding_origin' columns and add 'evaluation_trace' field to audit_events (DB migration + index plan).
Runtime: implement scope stack builder and evaluate permission engine with deterministic logging (feature-flagged).
Console: add Role Preview UI (show expanded permissions for a given user+resource), Breakglass flow, and scoped delegation controls.
E2E tests: policy fuzzing harness that generates random hierarchies and asserts deterministic outcomes; include regression suite for deny/allow precedence.
Migration: compatibility layer for RBAC v1 tokens for 8 weeks, telemetry to track mismatches, and rollback plan.
open_questions: Should explicit 'deny' be globally highest precedence or scoped-nearest highest? (proposal: nearest-scope deny outranks global allow).
How to represent attribute-based ephemeral grants in audit logs without leaking sensitive attribute values? (proposal: hash attributes and store policy id).
What is the retention period for evaluation_trace in audit_events given storage costs? (proposal: 90 days hot, 365 days cold).
Do we allow nested delegation (A delegates to B, B delegates to C) and how to limit blast radius?
How does breakglass interact with external identity providers' session policies and MFA requirements?
decisions: Adopt 'nearest-scope wins' for both allows and denies; explicit deny at a closer scope overrides allows at parent scopes.
SAML/OIDC claim mapping will be configurable per customer; default mappings provided for common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD).
Evaluation trace will include policy identifiers and decision outcomes; raw claim values will be redacted and represented by stable hashes.
risks: Incorrect precedence could accidentally grant access during the migration window; mitigated by compatibility mode and sampling telemetry.
Audit log volume will increase significantly when we log evaluation traces per request; require retention/aggregation plan.
Complex delegation chains introduce escalation paths; require approval workflows and delegation TTLs in UI.
